item.title: High-performance devices from lab-scale to micro module directed by vertical PbI2 homogeneous growth perovskite films
item.description:
Minhuan Wang, Yepin Zhao, Zhenyang Suo, Chenyue Wang, Pengfei Wang, Bingying Xu, Zhenhuang Su, Jiming Bian, et al.
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79173-6
Abstract The morphology of the initial PbI 2 film is very pivotal in dictating the uniformity and crystallinity of the resultant perovskite film in the two-step sequential deposition processes. A solution-based induction is introduced to transform PbI 2 clusters into PbI 2 nanowires to achieve controllable morphology of the PbI 2 film. The nanowires act as scaffolds for the subsequent perovskite formation. An in-plane low-angle diffraction detected in the in-situ grazing-incidence small-angle X-ray scattering (GISAXS) for the PbI 2 film indicates the formation of a periodically arranged ordered structure. The PbI 2 nanowires facilitate the ion-exchange process, markedly improving the homogeneity and orientation of the perovskite films, which is confirmed by the in-situ grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS). As a result, a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.94% (certified as 26.66%, a very high certification efficiency of n-i-p structured perovskite devices) is achieved for the laboratory area (aperture area of the mask is 0.0618 cm 2 ). Moreover, a micro module device with an aperture area of 21.54 cm 2 was successfully manufactured and achieved a PCE of 24.60% (certified as 24.02%).

item.title: A stem-like CD8+ T cell reservoir resists exhaustion and sustains alloimmunity a decade after transplantation
item.description:
Dawei Zou, Yulin Dai, Stephanie G. Yi, Shuang Li, Luan Truong, Lillian W. Gaber, Richard J. Knight, Xiang Xiao, et al.
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79209-x
Abstract Chronic antigen exposure is commonly thought to drive CD8 + T cells toward exhaustion. However, in transplantation, we show that sustained immunity is maintained by a persistent stem-like reservoir that iteratively replenishes short-lived cytotoxic effectors rather than progressing toward exhaustion. Analysis of rejected human kidney allografts obtained approximately 10 years after transplantation reveals extensive overlap of CD8 + T-cell clonotypes between the circulation and allografts. These clones are maintained in a TCF1 + stem-like state in the circulation but differentiate into TCF1 − cytotoxic effectors within allografts. Mouse models demonstrate that cytotoxic effector differentiation is restrained by TCF1 and depends on lactate dehydrogenase A. Cytotoxic effectors are short-lived and insufficient to mediate allograft rejection upon transfer into secondary hosts, whereas stem-like T cells retain self-renewal capacity, continuously replenish cytotoxic effectors, and drive rejection across serial transplantations. These findings establish a principle whereby a stem-like CD8 + T-cell reservoir drives sustained alloimmunity through continuous effector differentiation.

item.title: Layer-by-layer water filling in molecular-scale capillaries monitored by AFM
item.description:
Mingwei Chen, Jingshan Wang, Artem Mishchenko, Ivan Timokhin, Qi Ge, Fengchao Wang, Andre K. Geim, Qian Yang
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78542-5
Abstract Under ambient humidity, water spontaneously condenses in pores only a few nanometers in size, making nanoscale capillarity central to numerous natural phenomena and technological applications. At these dimensions, water may no longer be treated as a continuous fluid, yet the consequences of molecular discreteness for capillary condensation and filling remain poorly understood. Here we study two-dimensional (2D) nanocapillaries fabricated by van der Waals assembly and, using atomic force microscopy (AFM), monitor their wall deformations during humidity-driven water uptake. We observe two distinct regimes: layer-by-layer filling of flexible capillaries and abrupt filling of more rigid ones. Flexible walls deform in ≈3 Å steps, consistent with the entry of individual molecular layers of water. The different filling regimes are explained by a competition between wall deformation energy and oscillatory wall-water interactions. These results, together with the theoretical framework developed here, show how molecular discreteness can profoundly affect ubiquitous capillary phenomena, with wall rigidity determining whether this discreteness is exposed or hidden within an apparently classical, Kelvin-like response.

item.title: Molecular alloying of titanium–oxo clusters for linker-free S-scheme interfaces
item.description:
Dexin Wang, Guanyun Zhang, Lixia Xuan, Junshuo Nie, Juan Wang, Linping Liu, Yuting Li, Guo Wang, et al.
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78256-8
Abstract Heterojunction engineering is one of the most effective strategies for enhancing charge separation and improving the performance of photo-functional materials. However, such heterojunction functionality has been almost exclusively realized in extended solids, and how to translate this concept into atomically precise molecular systems remains an open question. Here, we employ two isostructural yet electronically distinct titanium-oxo clusters, Ti 12 Mn 6 O 18 (Bz) 30 and Ti 12 Cr 6 O 18 (Bz) 30 (denoted as TiMn and TiCr, respectively; Bz denotes C 6 H 5 CO 2 ), as modular nanosized building blocks to construct molecular alloys that form eutectic molecular alloys across the entire compositional range. Free from covalent or ionic linkages, TiMn and TiCr achieve spontaneous Fermi-level equilibration solely through intimate intermolecular packing, thereby establishing an S-scheme junction at the molecular scale. This markedly enhances charge-carrier separation, carrier lifetime, and interfacial charge-transport kinetics, leading to substantially increased photocurrents, accelerated reactive oxygen species generation, and significantly improved elimination of representative waterborne micropollutants. The emergent functionality originates from local electronic complementarity and low-resistance intermolecular charge-transport channels facilitated by ligand π–π interactions, whereas long-range crystalline order is not essential. Our findings suggest a convenient approach for developing nanocluster-level functional donor–acceptor systems without relying on extended frameworks or on covalent fusion between the building units.

item.title: Contrasting epigenetic dynamics in chromosome arms and pericentromeres during ROS1-induced plant immune memory
item.description:
Adam Hannan Parker, Peijun Zhang, Kwok Yin Man, Louis Tirot, Stephen A. Rolfe, Lisa M. Smith, Samuel W. Wilkinson, Jurriaan Ton
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78905-y
Abstract Immune memory enables plants to respond more effectively to recurrent pathogen infections. Epigenetic changes in DNA methylation and small RNAs have been implicated, yet how their temporal dynamics govern immune memory establishment and erasure remains unclear. Using a chemically inducible system to activate the DNA demethylase REPRESSOR OF SILENCING 1 (ROS1) in Arabidopsis, we establish immune memory against biotrophic pathogens that persists for at least one week. Memory establishment coincides with reduced small RNA accumulation and DNA methylation along chromosome arms, including at promoters of genes involved in salicylic acid–dependent immunity and DNA damage repair. These changes are progressively reversed during immune memory erasure. In contrast, transposon-rich pericentromeres retain elevated small RNA and DNA methylation levels, consistent with a CLASSY3-associated redistribution of RNA-directed DNA methylation. Our findings show that transient ROS1 activity drives contrasting epigenetic responses across chromosomal regions, shaping both the establishment and erasure of plant immune memory.

item.title: Neanderthal introgressed ancestry reveals human genomic regions enriched with recessive deleterious mutations
item.description:
Xinjun Zhang, Lingxuan Zhu, Jiongxuan Yang, Nina Sachdev, Jazlyn Mooney, Harold Z. Wang, Sriram Sankararaman, Kirk E. Lohmueller
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78708-1
Abstract Negative selection on deleterious mutations plays a key role in shaping human genetic variation, yet the dominance effects of these mutations remain poorly understood because existing statistical methods often cannot distinguish dominance effects from the overall selective effects. In this work, we take a fundamentally different approach by leveraging the distribution of Neanderthal ancestry across the human genome. Simulations show that recessive deleterious mutations can increase archaic introgressed ancestry through heterosis in the absence of positive selection, in contrast to the depletion expected under additive effects. We use this signal to develop DominL , a machine learning classifier trained on simulations of human demography with Neanderthal introgression to identify megabase-scale genomic windows enriched with recessive mutations. DominL demonstrates robust accuracy, with particularly high power in exon-dense regions. Applied to 7 non-African populations from the 1000 Genomes Project, DominL identifies approximately 3-9% of the genome as enriched for recessive mutations, with most high-confidence regions shared across populations. Predicted regions show patterns consistent with expected signatures from recessive mutations, including weakened background selection, depletion of runs of homozygosity, and enrichment of non-additive trait-associated variants. These regions also contain genes associated with metabolic and immune-related functions.

item.title: Scalable crosslinking-regulated membranes with ultra-high Li+/Mg2+ selectivity for lithium recovery from brines
item.description:
Zhen Wang, Guoshen Zeng, Yueyue Li, Changting Wang, Yang Liu, Bolun Peng, Jinhua Feng, Rongzhen Ma, et al.
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79061-z
Abstract Membrane-based separation has emerged as a competitive technology for lithium extraction from salt-lake brines. However, its industrial implementation remains limited by the low Li + /Mg 2+ selectivity of conventional membranes. In this work, we demonstrate that regulation of the crosslinking degree during membrane formation enables subnanometer pore size control within the narrow window required for Li + /Mg 2+ separation. Under electrodialysis conditions, the membrane achieved a Li + /Mg 2+ separation factor of up to 6454 at an Mg/Li mass ratio of 140, outperforming previously reported membranes for Li + /Mg 2+ separation. Importantly, the membrane maintained a Li + /Mg 2+ separation factor above 1200 in untreated natural salt-lake brine, despite the high Mg/Li mass ratio (Mg/Li = 87) and the presence of multiple competing ions. Fabrication of a 25 cm × 35 cm membrane and stable performance over 15 days of repeated operation further supported the practical viability of this approach. The practical membrane design strategy reported in this work can inspire the development of ion-selective membranes with precisely regulated subnanometer pores for a wide range of sustainable separation processes.

item.title: Reversal of trauma-induced monocyte paralysis by IFN-γ fails to prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia, implicating lymphoid deficits in infection risk
item.description:
Jonas Schmid, Susanne Unger, Athanasios Ziogas, Stefanie Kreutmair, Maud Mayoux, Can Ulutekin, Colin Sparano, Juan Villar-Vesga, et al.
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78844-8
Abstract Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) remains a frequent and severe complication in critically ill patients. Although interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) has been reported to restore trauma-associated immune defects, the PREV-HAP trial (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04793568) did not show a benefit of IFN-γ on VAP prevention. To investigate the immunological basis of this therapeutic failure, we performed longitudinal high-dimensional immunoprofiling on 104 trial participants. IFN-γ improved phenotypic and metabolic features of monocyte immune suppression, most notably by increasing HLA-DR expression. Whereas HLA-DR on monocytes is a well-established biomarker for patient outcomes, its modulation via IFN-γ injection did not prevent lung pathology, possibly due to CCR7 induction. In contrast, we identified pre-existing deficits in T- and B-cell subsets in patients who subsequently developed VAP. Together, these findings suggest that monocytic HLA-DR expression reflects the immune status rather than directly influencing VAP susceptibility, and that lymphoid immune alterations may represent more relevant determinants of infection risk in ventilated patients.

item.title: Exceptional bound states in the continuum in a passive terahertz metasurface
item.description:
Chen Chen, Ziyi Liu, Jianfei Li, Junhan Zhou, Yuanhang Jiang, Ying Wang, Zhongxiang Zhou, Hongyu Liu, et al.
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-78664-w
Abstract Exceptional bound states in the continuum (EP-BICs) are hybrid singularities in non-Hermitian systems that uniquely combine the non-radiating characteristic of bound states in the continuum (BICs) with the enhanced sensitivity of exceptional points (EPs). However, their experimental realization remains challenging because existing proposals typically require precise external excitation to control the loss and coupling strength. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an EP-BIC in a fully passive terahertz metasurface. Through simple geometric rotation, we modulate the internal coupling of two resonator modes to drive an isolated EP to coalesce with a line of BICs and finally form an EP-BIC, as clearly traced by transmission spectra measurements. Near-field terahertz scanning further observes the uniform phase distribution of EP-BIC, confirming its decoupling from incident light. Finally, the sensor performance of EP-BIC is demonstrated in water mist detection and exhibits a distinct dip response that enables unambiguous signal identification, in contrast to the weak and spectrally crowded peak of conventional EP. Our work establishes a practical and robust platform for EP-BICs, opening avenues for ultra-sensitive photonic sensing.

item.title: A nanocomposite-mediated synergistic division inhibition strategy for selective antibacterial therapy against burn infections
item.description:
Hao Liu, Zhixuan Yu, Ling Yang, Siyang Zhao, Tianzhi Li, Rui Li, Guanyu Ding, Ling Liu, et al.
Nature Communications
DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-79027-1
Abstract Nanomaterial-based antibacterial therapy presents an alternative solution to antibiotic resistance. However, most research focuses on enhancing antibacterial activity while neglecting the selectivity of nanomaterials, leading to indiscriminate damage to mammalian cells. Here, we design a synergistic boron nitride-polydopamine@MOF-199 nanocomposite (BPM NC) that interferes with bacterial binary fission. Its selectivity stems from suppressing FtsZ polymerization during bacterial division, while its high efficiency arises from synergistic mechanisms such as disrupting membrane potential and bacterial defense systems. These effects induce molecular-level disruptions in bacterial biological processes, enabling BPM NC (0.35 μg/mL) to rapidly inactivate bacteria (10 7 CFU/mL) in 30 min—358-fold enhancement over its precursor h-BN. In burn infection models, BPM NC exhibits significant efficacy in male mice and female pigs, outperforming the clinical drug silver sulfadiazine. This work provides a promising insight into developing antibacterial nanomaterials that combine selectivity and high activity, offering a strategy for next-generation antibacterial therapies.
